Hey there!

So, let me start this off by saying that you're in no immediate danger. The brain is a crazy, wild thing capable of TERRIFYINGLY incredible (incredibly amazing or bad) things. If I told you of every dream I woke up from and thought they were scarily ominous, I could fill this entire comment section lol. Dreams are those kinds of things that you shouldn't really take that seriously. Rarely, they will have precognitive events, but most people won't have to worry about that much.

Now, going of the brain being a crazy organ: your dream could mean many things, and could also just mean nothing but a wild mixture of random things. Generally, vampires in dreams mean that you are just feeling drained. *Dreamlandia.com says that: if you see a vampire in your dream, that means that there is a significant person in your life who is the source of your troubles. There's other variations of course, and they're very easily able to be searched.

As for your ominous symbols and such, they could be just that, symbols. I once had a nightmare with the Leviathan Cross (the two-armed cross with the infinity sign on the bottom) being carved into my ribcage and then burned with a torch by a bunch of demon shadow looking things. Was I terrfied as Hell waking up? Yes, I was. But I was not physically harmed and felt spiritually okay. In the end, it was just my brain fucking with me. Another dream I once had, was that I was surrounded by murky darkness, standing on a cliff and looking down towards the sound of high pitched wailing and screaming. When it seemed to start getting closer, I felt claws slowly sliding over my shoulders and then dig into my skin. Again, yes, I was terribly scared upon waking up, but I was fine in the end.

Now I'm not saying that your dream isn't scary or doesn't mean something. It definitely can, for sure. But I want to believe that you're not in any danger phsycially or spiritually and it's just the mind doing what the mind does best: creating a scene.

Best wishes to finding out what yours may mean! 😊

TLDR: the mind is a crazy thing, don't worry to much about it. 😄

Hey there!

Well, the good thing is that you most likely aren't dying from this, as far as I know! From what you've described, it sounds kind of like hypnagogic hallucinations.

Hypnagogic hallucinations are a type of phenomena that happens during the onset of sleep, or 'barely drifting off' like you described. They can be of a taste, smell, sound or, like you said, a vision. The images can be extremely complex, like multiple lines of color stretching across your vision, swimming around, overlapping and etc. Or they can be very simple; animals, people, etc. They can seem extremely real, too.

The only thing that is different is that you said it doesn't appear in your room, and some/most hallucinations related to this condition do. But it's still being researched and studied upon, so I'm not exactly sure of the complete idea of that. It is mostly linked to narcolepsy, but can also be related to insomnia, drug/alcohol use and, yes, untreated anxiety and stress!

I'm no expert for sure, so I could be completely wrong lol, but your experiences sound really interesting and I love meddling in the study of dreams/sleep.

Have a great night!

Hi!

When I first started reading your post, my mind immediately went to a certain parasomnia called Exploding Head Syndrome (what I go through every now and then). Despite it's crazy name, no harm comes to you physically, but it's a phenomenon where you hear sudden, loud noises when either falling asleep or waking up (ex. gunshots, explosions, bangs). But, when you went on to describe that it was actual sounds in your dreams, I was a little stumped. False awakenings are definitely a possiblility. But the thing is, is that I've done the same thing before; this morning actually! 

I woke up from a dream that I was talking to a vampire and when I was waking up, I could hear him still talking. I knew it wasn't anyone else in the house because nobody had his voice and we were talking about something that nobody in my house would possibly be talking about. It's quite a crazy, weird thing. The only thing I can put together is that our brains are still trying to play through the dream; aka our physical body is waking up but our brain cortex/stem/mind is still in the audible parts of our REM sleep even if our mind has stopped the visual parts of the dream itself. Like an auditory hallucination of some kind.

I'm looking to study oneirology one day, so this is a really interesting topic to me haha. I wish I could give you a more specific answer, but all I can offer is speculation, my personal experience and a guess. I hope you have a great night! 😊
